acknowledge_unwitnessed.reason: Level 0, the factory value (RM0433 Rev 9 Table 21, p. 177), so FAB-NOTES carries no step; no model, the twin presents it (4230 FEEDBACK section 2 m1). The bench row reads bits 3:2 as 00.
PA5-PA7 at AF5 for SPI1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back.
PA0 output (flash CS) and PA5-PA7 alternate for SPI1: a BSRR write drives a pin whatever MODER says (4200 FEEDBACK). The bench row reads MODER back.
PA0 and SPI1's PA5-PA7: no edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges each chosen speed's fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10, measured): written whole, push-pull on every port A pin. The bench row reads it back.
No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no pull on the solved pins, the debug pins' reset pulls (PA13 up, PA14 down, PA15 up) kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
PB6/PB7 at AF4 for I2C1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back.
PB6/PB7 alternate for I2C1: the model routes a pin by MODER only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads MODER back.
PB6/PB7 for I2C1 at 400 kHz: no edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges the chosen speed's fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10): PB6/PB7 open-drain for I2C1, the rest push-pull. The bench row reads it back.
No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no internal pull on PB6/PB7 (the bus has 2.2 kOhm), PB4's reset pull-up kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
PE is set by the enable, not by silicon::i2c_cr1 (whose word has PE clear); stored, with no reaction claimed. The bench row reads PE as 1.
7-bit addressing, no reload, no PEC, written 0 (AUTOEND set at run time): STM32F7_I2C.cs is not held, no reaction claimed. The bench row reads CR2 back, all but AUTOEND.
Write-1-to-clear (RM0433 Rev 9 section 47.9.8, p. 2015), so no bench row: STOPCF and NACKCF after each transfer. The next record's OK status on silicon shows the clear took.
Not polled (ruling on Q-F): STM32H7_RCC.cs L175 keeps it a tag reading 0, so a wait would park every boot. Silicon must read 1 after a D2 enable: a bench row.
A tag in Renode (STM32H7_RCC.cs L401, read 0 whatever is written, 4230 FEEDBACK section 2). SPI1's kernel per_ck assumes HSI here; the bench row reads it.
ResetClock reads them at reset before the select write; a tag (STM32H7_RCC.cs L408-410) reads 0 whatever silicon holds. The written SPI123SEL is judged by spi_words.
Left at reset: I2C123SEL's rcc_pclk1 is what check_timingr assumes; ResetClock reads the USART selects though no port uses them. A tag in Renode (L420-425); the bench row reads each.
The FPU enable in the generated Reset, outside every Kani harness; whether Renode faults a float with CPACR clear is not held. The bench row reads CP10/CP11 as full access.
A tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L149), written 0 with TSIZE: no reload is used. The bench row reads it back as 0.
Tags in Renode (STM32H7_SPI.cs L258-266), written 0 beside EOTC; write-only, so no bench row. The boot record's flash identity, read on silicon, shows each transfer ended.
MODF is a tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L238) and MASTER always reads 1: no mode fault in the twin. SSM|SSI before SPE is proved by Kani; the bench row reads MODF as 0.
